ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an arrow-pushing mechanism of an organoaluminum reagent and an alkynyl alcohol derivative. The aluminum atom is connected to H, two R groups, and O; O is further connected to the chiral carbon on the right side, and this carbon is also connected to R1 and an alkynyl fragment. A curved arrow shows the Al-H bond, as an electron/hydride source, pointing to the left-side carbon of the alkyne bond, and another arrow shows the alkyne bond π electrons moving toward the adjacent carbon. Reasoning: After moving the electrons according to the arrows, H is added to the left-side/terminal alkyne carbon, and C≡C is reduced to C=C; transfer of the π electrons makes the vinyl carbon on the side close to the chiral carbon carry a negative charge. The right-side chiral carbon and its O-Al connection and wildcard R groups remain unchanged. Therefore the SMILES corresponding to the product state is [*]/C([H])=[C-]/[C@@H](O[Al]([*])[*])[*].

raw_record.question_text: An 'arrow-pushing' diagram is a common type of chemical image used to illustrate electron flow in mechanistic steps. Please choose the SMILES expression for the molecules(state) after the electron has been relocated, as depicted in the image. <image_1>

method.method_draft: First describe the image and identify the electron-flow arrows. Treat the Al-H bond as the hydride electron source and the alkyne as the acceptor. Apply the arrows: form a C-H bond on the left/terminal alkyne carbon, reduce the C≡C to C=C, and place the negative charge on the adjacent vinylic carbon. Keep the chiral carbon attached to O-Al and wildcard substituent unchanged. Convert the resulting vinyl anion/aluminum alkoxide state into SMILES with wildcard R groups and the shown E/Z and chiral annotations, yielding the target form [*]/C([H])=[C-]/[C@@H](O[Al]([*])[*])[*].
